title: Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty: analysis of clinical outcomes of patients with 8–10 years follow-up

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License); public

groups.description: DMEK performed July 2009 to June 2012 (single centre); the 66 of 450 operated eyes that met the inclusion criterion of at least 8 years of follow-up. Indications: Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy 60 eyes, DMEK after failed DSAEK 4 eyes, DMEK after failed DMEK 2 eyes (repeat grafts reported as indications of the cohort, so indication mixed). Triple DMEK (DMEK combined with cataract surgery) in 28 of the 66 eyes (combined left null: only part of the group).

notes: Retrospective consecutive single-centre case series. Inclusion criterion: minimum postoperative follow-up of 8 years, shorter than the last tabulated visit (10 years), so the group is kept with this note (addendum 2); 66 of 450 operated eyes qualified; participation in all intermediate visits was not required.
Four eyes had graft failure after the 8-year visit and repeat DMEK at 101-127 months; the article does not state how they enter the later means.
Per-eye follow-up data and graft survival of all 450 eyes are in supplementary files, which are not acquired (addendum 1); group means of the article's own Table 1 are extracted.
Endothelial cell density and central corneal thickness (Table 2) are tabulated: notes only.
Extracted under extraction protocol 1.0.0, the extraction brief and addendum 1 (development extractor D5).
